memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "With your own eyes you saw those great trials, those signs and great wonders. But to this day the Lord has not given you a mind that understands or eyes that see or ears that hear." — Deut 29:3-4 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
Here Moses says something startling. The people had seen God's great signs and wonders with their own eyes — yet "to this day the Lord has not given you a mind that understands or eyes that see or ears that hear." They had witnessed the miracles, but they had not truly grasped them. There is a kind of seeing that never reaches the heart.

This is a sobering truth. It is possible to be surrounded by evidence of God's power and still not really understand. A person can hear the gospel a hundred times, sit in church for years, know all the facts, and yet remain spiritually blind. True understanding is not merely intellectual; it is a gift that God must give.

That should keep us humble and prayerful. We cannot manufacture spiritual sight by our own cleverness. We need God to open our eyes, to soften our hearts, to help us truly see and hear. Even our understanding of Him is a gift of grace.

The wonderful news is that this is exactly what God delights to give. Jesus opened blind eyes as a sign of the deeper sight He came to bring. Paul prays that God would give us "the eyes of your heart" enlightened to know Him (Eph 1:18). If you long to understand God more deeply, ask Him. He is the one who gives the seeing eye and the hearing ear. Do not rely on your own insight — pray for His light to open your heart.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Have I been exposed to God's truth without letting it reach my heart?
2. Am I depending on my own understanding, or asking God to open my eyes?
3. What would it look like to pray for spiritual sight this week?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Lord, open the eyes of my heart. I cannot understand You by my own cleverness — I need Your light. Give me a mind that understands, eyes that see, and ears that hear. Amen.
